text: For most of human history, the deadliest thing in your environment wasn't a predator. It was a parasite carried by a mosquito.
G six P D is an enzyme that keeps your red blood cells stable under chemical stress. Reduce it, and those cells become fragile.
Which is exactly the problem, if you are a malaria parasite trying to live inside one.

A parasite inside a G six P D deficient red cell creates stress the cell can't absorb. The cell gets damaged and cleared early. And the parasite goes with it. Your body doesn't kill the invader. It demolishes the building.

G six P D deficiency is one of the most common enzyme deficiencies on Earth. Somewhere around four hundred million people. Its distribution overlaps strongly with regions where malaria has historically been intense.
And here is where the bill finally arrives in full.

Those fragile red cells are fragile for everything, not just parasites. Certain medications, certain infections, and fava beans can push them to break down in large numbers at once. The word for that is hemolytic anemia. And for someone who doesn't know they're deficient, it can be genuinely dangerous.

Even the protection is uneven. Research has found deficiency lowering the risk of one severe malaria outcome, while appearing to raise another. There is no clean answer, because there was never a clean trade.
Every other gene in this video handed you something and quietly filed the invoice somewhere. This one hands you the invoice at the same time.
Evolution didn't build a perfect defense here. It struck a bargain, and it took the terms it could get.
